D0.name: empiricalMean
D0.declaration:
noncomputable def empiricalMean (y : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ t ∈ Finset.range n, y t) / n

D1.name: meanPredict
D1.declaration:
noncomputable def meanPredict (y : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if t = 0 then 1/2 else empiricalMean y t

D2.name: expectedFixedMinimum
D2.declaration:
noncomputable def expectedFixedMinimum {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) (Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (T : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  sInf ((fun u : ℝ => ∫ ω, ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, (u - Y t ω)^2 ∂μ) ''
    Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)

D3.name: expectedFixedRegret
D3.declaration:
noncomputable def expectedFixedRegret {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) (Y prediction : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (T : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (∫ ω, ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, (prediction t ω - Y t ω)^2 ∂μ) -
    expectedFixedMinimum μ Y T

propositions.header:
theorem expected_fixed_prefix_decomposition {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hY : ∀ t, Measurable (Y t))
    (hlaw : ∀ t, IdentDistrib (Y t) (Y 0) μ μ)
    (hb : ∀ t, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Y t ω ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (T : ℕ) (u : ℝ) :
    (∫ ω, ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, (u - Y t ω)^2 ∂μ) =
      (T : ℝ) * variance (Y 0) μ +
        (T : ℝ) * (u - ∫ ω, Y 0 ω ∂μ)^2

propositions.header:
theorem history_policy_expectedFixed_excess {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (Y : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hY : ∀ t, Measurable (Y t))
    (hlaw : ∀ t, IdentDistrib (Y t) (Y 0) μ μ)
    (hb : ∀ t, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Y t ω ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
    (hind : iIndepFun Y μ)
    (policy : (t : ℕ) → ((↑(Finset.range t) : Type) → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ t, Measurable (policy t))
    (hpb : ∀ t z, (∀ i, z i ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) →
      policy t z ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (T : ℕ) :
    expectedFixedRegret μ Y (fun t ω => policy t (fun i => Y i ω)) T =
      (∑ t ∈ Finset.range T,
        ∫ ω, (policy t (fun i => Y i ω) - ∫ ω, Y 0 ω ∂μ)^2 ∂μ) ∧
      0 ≤ expectedFixedRegret μ Y (fun t ω => policy t (fun i => Y i ω)) T

sevenSlotReview.assessment: Source scalar predictions/outcomes in[0,1] are real RVs on arbitrary measurable Omega with probability mu and AE interval support. D2 comparator remains a deterministic real constant. Q005 policy has finite strict-history tuple domain. General vector V-regret context is not represented by these eight claims and is not claimed covered.

One law and one deterministic comparator across all times/outcomes. Natural source round t+1 maps to Lean t. All Y/hY/hlaw/hb conditions quantify globally over N, although each conclusion uses range T; this is an infinite-stream representation, not claimed equivalent to every arbitrary finite-only input without extension. Q005/8 policy is supplied before horizon, uses exactly coordinates i<t, and no current target is passed.

Probability/measurability formalize implicit random-variable regularity. Same marginal law alone suffices Q001-3/7; independence is removed where unnecessary, a supported generalization. Q004's L2 and pair independence are explicit consumer premises. Q005/6 produce them from source IID and deterministic measurable legal-history behavior. Q008 retains unused source-context hind/hp/hpb. No lower-bound/minimizer/cross-term identity/convergence is assumed.

Q001 gives fixed-loss bias-variance identity; Q002 actual feasible mean and least value; Q003 infimum equals T variance; Q004 independent random-prediction identity; Q005/6 deterministic causal producer identity and nonnegativity; Q007 oracle zero excess; Q008 finite normalization. These are derived support facts for the source assertions, not eight newly printed source theorems.

Exactly T terms indexed0..T-1, variance multiplied by real T, comparator interval[0,1]. meanPredict starts1/2 then divides strict-prefix sum by t. Only Q008 excludes T0. Q008 subtracts variance outside loss/T. T0 extension is explicit in other claims; no uniqueness at T0. No changed constants or erased boundary terms.

Minimum stays outside expectation. Q004 permits any L2 prediction independent of current Y, without asserting it is causal. Q005/6 are actual deterministic causal constructions. No private random seed, random kernel, external-information or completed-filtration class is represented. Known population mean is an oracle comparison, not an unknown-law learner.

Total Lean integral/sInf definitions on arbitrary inputs do not promise ordinary finite expectations, attainment, or nonnegativity. Source-domain theorem hypotheses supply those meanings. AE support is not pointwise; policy feasibility is legal-tuples only, though measurability is on the full real-tuple domain. Finite normalization is not natural-sequence convergence, little-o, a rate or uniform comparator no-regret.

declarationReview.interpretation: Total finite arithmetic mean. Empty-prefix value0 is explicit extension; no interval feasibility for arbitrary real input.
Initial1/2 then strict-past mean. Not defined on source pp1-2, retained only as an explicitly derived existing-library instantiation.
Real sInf of image of[0,1] under expected cumulative fixed loss; neither pathwise min nor adaptive comparator. Q002 supplies IsLeast and witness mean before Q003 uses csInf_eq.
Expected supplied prediction loss minus D2. No causality/range/sign encoded in definition. Cheating canary gives negative value.

declarationReview.delta: No joint independence and arbitrary u are valid algebraic generalizations. L2 is produced from measurable AE support.
Feasibility plus least objective value is stronger than a bare numeric infimum. Actual proof names population mean witness. No uniqueness asserted.
sInf representation becomes actual minimum value via Q002; no assumed minimizer or default-value certificate.
hP/hInd restrict arbitrary supplied prediction, not a complete source causal class. Its source use is through Q005/6 which discharge those premises.
Global measurable history functions with feasible outputs on legal tuples, AE outcomes. Explicit subclass excludes seeds/randomized/general-filtration strategies.
Algorithm-specific derived instance outside literal pp1-2 definitions. No sample-mean consistency or convergence imported from its name.
Known population mean attains benchmark. Zero excess does not mean zero loss and is not an unknown-law algorithm.
Positive natural T essential. Boundaries explicitly state no asymptotic claim. hind/hp/hpb retained but not needed for algebraic equality.

Q001 deterministic bias-variance; Q002 bounded expectation and mean witness; Q003 IsLeast.csInf_eq; Q007 attained zero excess.
Q005/Q006 actual finite deterministic history and mean policies supply independence/L2 internally and prove nonnegative expected-fixed excess.
